item.text: I’ll read the notes, group their answers by question, write the map, and run the required check.

item.aggregated_output:
<<15:76 notes, part 0 of 0..0>>
[MUJAHID:v1p342#5/r1] MUJAHID, d. 104 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the site lay beside a clearly marked road.
[MUQATIL:15:74-77/r4] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Lot's ruined towns lie on a clear, enduring route between Mecca and Syria that Meccans and others travel.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p184/r5] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | The remains of the town lie by a clear, evident road.
[THALABI:v5p345/r22] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The destroyed towns of Lot remained beside a clear, permanent road.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r1] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as enduring destruction.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r2] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid glosses it as lying on a marked road.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p168/r3] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | holds | The pronoun refers to the people of Lot’s towns and the people of the Thicket, Shuʿayb’s community.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | “It” refers to the city of Lot’s people, mentioned earlier in 15:67. | mentions 15:67
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says the city lies on your people’s road toward Syria, a familiar route.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · قتادة ومجاهد والضحاك | reports | Qatada, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak take the phrase as a clear road that is neither obliterated nor hidden, remaining open to travelers.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p639/r4] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | holds | The persistent traces make it possible to take a lesson from the city.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:15:75-81/r2] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Lot's town lies on a lasting, unmistakable road that Quraysh take toward Syria.
[JISHUMI:v6p3973/r1] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الحسن، وقتادة، والضحاك، ومجاهد | reports | The signs and the settled route are clear to people who have seen the remains and heard the reports about Lot's people.
[JISHUMI:v6p3973/r10] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The remains endure so people can learn from them, and they provide divine لطف for us.
[JISHUMI:v6p3973/r2] JISHUMI, d. 494 · الأصم، وأبو علي | reports | Alternatively, the signs are known and enduring.
[JISHUMI:v6p3973/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · قتادة | reports | Qatāda locates the dwellings of Lot's people between Medina and Syria.
[JISHUMI:v6p3973/r8] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The verses show that Lot's people were destroyed and the believing members of his household were saved.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The towns of Lot lie beside a clear, established road.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p388/r7] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says the road is marked and cannot be hidden or disappear.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r14] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد وقتادة وابن زيد | reports | Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd take the pronoun to refer to the destroyed city, on a clear, known route.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p370/r15] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The pronoun might instead refer to the signs or the stones; the latter is supported by a report that punishment stones hang between heaven and earth, whose quotation is cut off in the source.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p371/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | The clipped opening preserves a quoted fragment mentioning the earth, two thousand years, and sinners of the Prophet’s community, but its full claim is not recoverable here.
[RAZI-FULL:v19p161/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The pronoun in “it is on an enduring road” returns to Lot's city; its visible, undimmed ruins remain on the route from the Ḥijāz to Syria.
[QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r1] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The feminine pronoun refers to the towns of Lot's people.
[QURTUBI-FULL:15:76-79/r2] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | They lie on a lasting road your people take toward Syria.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:15:75-80/r2] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | The city or villages lie beside a permanent, well-traveled road whose traces people see.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The pronoun means the towns' visible remains on a fixed route, still seen and not erased.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p246#3/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The ruins warn Quraysh, as does the reminder that they pass destroyed towns morning and night. | mentions 37:137, 37:138
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r23] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · مجاهد، قتادة، ابن زيد | reports | Mujahid, Qatada, and Ibn Zayd take the pronoun in وإنها as the destroyed city, which lies on a visible road for those who reflect.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r24] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غير مسمى | reports | Other possibilities are that وإنها refers to the signs or the stones.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r25] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غير مسمى | reports | A further view makes the pronoun refer to the cry, lying in wait for anyone who repeats the people’s deeds; the author links it to the verse saying it is not far from wrongdoers.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r26] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | لبسبيل means a fixed, visible passage that has not disappeared, allowing people to see it and learn from it.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p490/r27] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The preserved route warns Quraysh because they pass by the ruins in the morning and at night.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r1] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The continuation quotes that the cry is not far from wrongdoers, supporting the preceding interpretation that it awaits those who repeat their deeds.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r2] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · غير مسمى | reports | مقيم may mean known, or it may mean lasting and continuous.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p491/r3] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas glosses the lasting route as an enduring way of destruction.
[SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | prefers | The apparent referent of the pronoun is the city or the towns.
[SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | Another proposed referent for the pronoun is the stones.
[SAMIN-DURR:15:76/r3] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | A further proposed referent for the pronoun is the signs.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The ruined town of Sodom, overturned physically and morally and pelted with stones until it became a foul lake, lies beside a clear, well-traveled route that remains in use.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The established route beside the town is linked to the statement that people pass the destroyed cities morning and night. | mentions 37:137, 37:138
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · مجاهد والضحاك | reports | Mujahid and al-Dahhak gloss the phrase as meaning that the route is marked or recognizable.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r5] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · قتادة | reports | Qatada explains the route as clear and open.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r6] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · قتادة | reports | Qatada also says the place is in a single region of the earth.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p544/r7] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · السدي | rejects | Al-Suddi takes the phrase to mean that Sodom is in a manifest register, as in 36:12, but Ibn Kathir says that is not the intended sense here. | mentions 36:12
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r11] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | An imām here is a clear, enduring path that people follow; it displays God’s greatness and defense of his messengers, and its traces have not vanished.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r12] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The passage uses ihtibāk: “fixed” in the first description implies “clear” omitted there, while “clear” in the second implies “fixed” omitted there.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p231/r6] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The overturned cities remain on a clear, fixed road, making reflection easy; Quraysh passed them on some journeys to Syria.
[DURR-FULL:v5p91/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the place’s being on a lasting road as a route to destruction.
[DURR-FULL:v5p91/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · مجاهد | reports | Mujāhid instead explains the phrase as a clear, well-known road.
[BURSEVI:v4p319#3/r3] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The ruined towns remain beside a stable, traveled route between Mecca and Syria, so Quraysh should take warning when journeying to Syria because their traces have not disappeared.
[ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | The pronoun may refer to the destroyed city or the destroyed towns.
[ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The phrase means they lie on a fixed road that people travel and where they can see the ruins.
[ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r3] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · قيل | reports | Other proposed antecedents are the signs, stones, or cry; if the cry, it lies in wait for those who act as they did. | mentions 11:83
[ALUSI-FULL:v14p74#4/r4] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | reports | Muqīm is glossed as known or lasting, continually traveled along.
[ASAD-NOTES:15:75#n55/r1] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Asad identifies the road as running from northern Hijaz to Syria along the Dead Sea; aerial photographs published by the American School of Oriental Research confirmed its trace.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p290/r3] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | The expression sabīl muqīm means a commonly trodden way.
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p290/r4] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Quraysh are urged to learn from ruined nations, whose remains they pass on trade routes; Sodom and Gomorrah lay on the Hijaz–Syria route.
[STUDYQURAN:15:75/r2] STUDYQURAN · Aj | reports | The standing path is a traveled road where people can see the vestiges of Lot’s destroyed people.

<<end of notes>>
